status_definitions.implemented: A mechanism present in this repository; its limits and tests remain authoritative. This label is not a performance claim.
status_definitions.experimental: Executable implementation with recorded limitations and validation; the adaptive learner uses this status even though adaptive is the constructor default. Choose policy=threads, policy=process or policy=hints to avoid learning.
status_definitions.planned: Design or research proposal only; not a supported runtime feature.

reference_note: References identify primary-source foundations or inspiration. The proposed mechanisms and benchmark designs are original project designs, not claims that the cited project implements them.

concepts.title: Bounded admission
concepts.mechanism: Bound both logical unfinished tasks and physically retained owned-queued plus dispatched scheduling items by max_pending; each backend dispatches at most its worker budget.
concepts.applicability: Producers that can outpace workers and retain large argument graphs.
concepts.risks: A count bound does not bound bytes, blocked producers, caller-retained Futures/results, or worker allocations. A cancelled dispatched thread item retains its physical slot until backend acknowledgement. Reentrant submission or blocking completion callbacks can deadlock.
concepts.benchmark_method: Hold workers behind a barrier, fill the admission budget, and verify the next submission waits or times out. Release tasks and assert capacity is reclaimed after success, failure, and cancellation.

concepts.title: Explicit thread and process hints
concepts.mechanism: Use TaskHints.kind and the explicit process_safe declaration to constrain backend selection before learned preferences are considered. ProcessPolicy supplies a deterministic process-only route that rejects absent backend or per-task consent without fallback.
concepts.applicability: Applications whose authors understand their I/O, CPU work, process importability, and state-sharing requirements.
concepts.risks: CPU is a workload hint rather than proof that processes help. process_safe is an author assertion, not a security sandbox or serialization guarantee.
concepts.benchmark_method: Use importable functions returning process IDs and deterministic outputs. Test CPU, I/O, unknown, and ineligible-process cases separately; compare outputs before timings.

concepts.title: Per-key backend EWMA selection
concepts.mechanism: Keep per-key backend completion records and uncontended completion EWMA; combine eligible observations with immutable owned-queue/dispatch-slot pressure, per-key bounded exploration and a switching deadband. Built-in policy templates create isolated executor state.
concepts.applicability: Repeated, reasonably comparable tasks with stable explicit keys.
concepts.risks: Uncontended observations still include startup and transfer overhead; slot occupancy is not CPU utilisation. Keys must group comparable tasks, observations can be stale, and pressure-adjusted scores are heuristics rather than service or completion-time guarantees.
concepts.benchmark_method: Feed controlled observations to policy unit tests, then run repeated comparable real workloads with separate cold and warm phases. Compare against fixed routes and report learning cost.

concepts.title: Execution profile records
concepts.mechanism: Record backend and measured completion information under task keys for inspection and policy feedback.
concepts.applicability: Explaining decisions and diagnosing workloads that behave differently than their supplied hints.
concepts.risks: An aggregate is not a profiler: it cannot isolate CPU time, I/O time, transfer cost, or causal bottlenecks. Admission time is excluded. Bounded keys can still expose business context, and callbacks can lag result availability.
concepts.benchmark_method: Inject successful and failing tasks, then verify recorded keys, backend counts, and nonnegative timings. Separate any diagnostics overhead from task runtime.

concepts.title: Cancellation propagation
concepts.mechanism: Return executor-owned standard Futures connected to removable pending items. Successful queued cancellation releases the payload; thread dispatch cancellation retains physical capacity until acknowledgement, while process Futures become running at dispatch.
concepts.applicability: Callers abandoning pending work and shutdown paths that cancel pending futures.
concepts.risks: Running work is not preempted; process work can be non-cancellable before callable entry. Wait timeouts do not cancel tasks. Explicit context management or shutdown(wait=True) is required for orderly accepted-work drain.
concepts.benchmark_method: Block a worker, cancel queued work, and verify it never enters its callable. Race cancel against start; ensure wait and as_completed observe terminal cancellation.

concepts.title: Standard Future interoperability
concepts.mechanism: Return genuine executor-owned concurrent.futures.Future objects supporting result, exception, cancel, wait, as_completed and done callbacks.
concepts.applicability: Incremental adoption by callers using submit, result, wait, as_completed, and context-managed shutdown.
concepts.risks: Future API compatibility does not imply identical stdlib callback threads, submission/map buffering or implicit interpreter-exit semantics. Normal completion callbacks are serialized on an owned pump and must not wait on another same-executor Future, even with free worker slots.
concepts.benchmark_method: Run compatibility tests for return values, keyword forwarding, exceptions, callbacks, mixed futures, cancellation, and shutdown across supported Python versions.

concepts.title: Explicit policy registry
concepts.mechanism: Use a per-instance PolicyRegistry of named factories; instantiate a custom registered policy and pass the resulting object to IntelligentExecutor. Built-in names are threads, hints, and adaptive.
concepts.applicability: Comparing policies and adding workload-specific choices without rewriting execution plumbing.
concepts.risks: Custom policy code executes inside the application and can block or fail; registration is not sandboxing, automatic package discovery, or compatibility certification.
concepts.benchmark_method: Register a minimal deterministic policy, resolve it by name, exercise invalid names, and verify the core still applies backend eligibility checks.

concepts.title: Input-size-aware profiles
concepts.mechanism: Explicit bounded numeric feature summaries partition immutable versioned workload profiles by exact feature equality; no raw input inspection. Implemented in prediction.py and submit_profiled.
concepts.applicability: The same operation over tiny and large payloads where process-transfer economics differ.
concepts.risks: Caller summaries can disclose private information; exact feature buckets can be sparse. Imported measurements do not prove future performance. No automatic feature engineering or learned interpolation.
concepts.benchmark_method: Sweep payload size and plot route choice and latency against fixed-backend crossovers. Hold out sizes and measure bucket overhead.

concepts.title: Cold-start-aware routing
concepts.mechanism: Separate pool-startup and import costs from steady-state observations, then consider expected remaining work before paying startup cost.
concepts.applicability: Short scripts and intermittent request bursts.
concepts.risks: Warmth is not binary, imports vary, and hidden prewarming can consume resources unexpectedly.
concepts.benchmark_method: Run fresh-interpreter single-task and batch trials, then persistent-pool trials. Report first-result and full-batch latency separately.

concepts.title: Bounded exploration budget
concepts.mechanism: Extend current interval-based exploration with a hard per-key or per-run budget on exploratory decisions or estimated added latency. The existing interval alone is not such a budget.
concepts.applicability: Repeated safe work where learning could otherwise impose unbounded user-visible cost.
concepts.risks: Low exploration misses changes; high exploration hurts latency. Never duplicate a task merely to obtain a counterfactual sample.
concepts.benchmark_method: Use workload phases with known fixed-route winners and measure cumulative excess latency, exploration count, and constraint violations.

concepts.title: Concept-drift detection
concepts.mechanism: Detect sustained changes in recent versus historical observations and age out or reset affected key profiles.
concepts.applicability: Changing payloads, network conditions, host load, or function implementations.
concepts.risks: Ordinary variance can trigger resets; an undetected regime change leaves stale decisions in control.
concepts.benchmark_method: Introduce a controlled change halfway through a replay and record detection delay, false resets, and time to recover baseline performance.

concepts.title: Uncertainty-aware selection
concepts.mechanism: Track sample counts and dispersion alongside means, declining to prefer a route when evidence is too sparse or noisy.
concepts.applicability: High-variance task families and infrequent keys.
concepts.risks: Latency observations are correlated and heavy-tailed; naive confidence formulas can overstate certainty.
concepts.benchmark_method: Use repeated seeded variable-duration trials and inspect selection stability, empirical error, and reporting overhead.

concepts.title: Queue-aware routing
concepts.mechanism: Use immutable per-backend owned-queued and occupied-dispatch counts with explicit task hints and uncontended completion observations; a pressure gap can redirect eligible work and a deadband limits noisy switching.
concepts.applicability: Mixed bursts where the historically faster backend has a long queue.
concepts.risks: Dispatch-slot utilisation is not CPU utilisation. Uncontended completion timings include startup/serialization, so pressure-adjusted ranking is heuristic. Predictive admission remains global and may idle another backend; no work-conserving or optimal routing guarantee.
concepts.benchmark_method: Inject staggered CPU and I/O bursts, record queue occupancy and p95 latency, and compare with the same service-only policy.

concepts.title: Failure-aware policy feedback
concepts.mechanism: Extend the current exclusion of failed latency samples into explicit failure-rate-aware selection with application-versus-backend failure classification.
concepts.applicability: Transient backend problems or task families with heterogeneous failure rates.
concepts.risks: Application errors do not necessarily implicate the backend; route changes must not retry side effects automatically.
concepts.benchmark_method: Inject distinct application and backend failures, verify classification, and compare successful throughput with raw task throughput.

concepts.title: Adaptive concurrency control
concepts.mechanism: Adjust effective admission or dispatch concurrency slowly using latency and resource-pressure feedback.
concepts.applicability: Workloads whose useful concurrency changes under external load.
concepts.risks: Controller instability, delayed feedback, and interaction with other autoscalers can make performance worse.
concepts.benchmark_method: Sweep fixed concurrency first; then test step changes and burst traces, recording overshoot, settling time, p95, and resource use.

concepts.title: Byte-weighted admission
concepts.mechanism: Combine the task-count bound with caller-supplied payload weights and a total outstanding-byte budget.
concepts.applicability: Large heterogeneous payloads that make a count-only bound inadequate.
concepts.risks: Weights omit copies and worker allocations; a caller can underestimate them. Defining release time matters for memory safety.
concepts.benchmark_method: Mix small and large buffers, measure peak resident memory and admission delay, and compare predicted versus observed memory.

concepts.title: Tenant-weighted fairness
concepts.mechanism: Allocate admission and dispatch credits to explicit application groups using weighted fair service.
concepts.applicability: A service sharing one executor across request classes or tenants.
concepts.risks: Fairness at task count differs from fairness at CPU cost; identities and weights become application policy.
concepts.benchmark_method: Run competing heavy and light producers and publish per-group throughput, p95, starvation intervals, and unused capacity.

concepts.title: Deadline-aware admission
concepts.mechanism: Reject or defer work whose estimated queue plus execution time exceeds an explicitly supplied deadline.
concepts.applicability: Latency-sensitive requests whose result has no value after a known time.
concepts.risks: Estimates can reject useful work or admit impossible deadlines. A deadline does not authorize interrupting external side effects.
concepts.benchmark_method: Use a deadline trace with known durations; measure deadline-goodput, false rejection, and wasted completed work.

concepts.title: Priority with aging
concepts.mechanism: Introduce priority queues with bounded aging so old low-priority tasks eventually make progress.
concepts.applicability: Interactive and bulk jobs sharing finite capacity.
concepts.risks: Priority inversion can persist through dependencies or external locks; preemption is not provided by queue reordering.
concepts.benchmark_method: Continuously submit urgent jobs around a long-lived background stream and verify a maximum starvation bound.

concepts.title: Per-resource rate limits
concepts.mechanism: Apply token-bucket admission keyed by an explicit external resource before occupying execution capacity.
concepts.applicability: APIs or databases with contractual request limits.
concepts.risks: Process-local limits do not enforce global quotas across services; retry and burst semantics must match the remote contract.
concepts.benchmark_method: Use a local fake service with quota enforcement and verify time-window request counts, burst size, and worker occupancy.

concepts.title: Burst reservation pools
concepts.mechanism: Reserve a small configurable capacity slice for short interactive jobs and lend it to bulk work only under safe rules.
concepts.applicability: Interactive latency requirements during scheduled bulk imports.
concepts.risks: Reservations reduce utilization, and long borrowed jobs may occupy capacity when an interactive burst arrives.
concepts.benchmark_method: Replay interactive arrivals over saturated bulk work; publish idle reservation cost and interactive tail latency.

concepts.title: Reentrant submission guard
concepts.mechanism: Detect attempts by pool workers to block while submitting into the same bounded executor and provide a clear diagnostic or opt-in fail-fast rule.
concepts.applicability: Nested parallel functions and accidental recursive use.
concepts.risks: Thread-local detection misses cross-executor cycles and process boundaries; inline fallback changes semantics.
concepts.benchmark_method: Construct one-worker and full-capacity nested submissions in subprocess tests with hard watchdogs; require deterministic diagnostics.

concepts.title: Bounded streaming map
concepts.mechanism: Provide map_bounded for one iterable with ordered output and a buffersize limit on submitted-but-unconsumed results. Closing the iterator attempts to cancel buffered work that has not started.
concepts.applicability: Large or infinite input streams and consumers slower than workers.
concepts.risks: Ordered output can retain completed results behind one slow item; iterator abandonment needs cleanup semantics.
concepts.benchmark_method: Use an instrumented infinite generator and slow consumer to bound read-ahead, retained results, and cancellation after early exit.

concepts.title: Small-task batching
concepts.mechanism: map_batches submits one explicit tuple chunk to a caller-supplied batch function per Future, yielding one result per batch. No hidden duplicate execution or retry.
concepts.applicability: Numerous tiny pure transformations with compatible error and cancellation requirements.
concepts.risks: Batching couples failure and cancellation; completed side effects cannot be rolled back, and running chunks cannot be partially cancelled. Result shape belongs to the batch callable. No hard memory bound.
concepts.benchmark_method: Sweep batch size against task duration and payload bytes; report throughput, first result, p95, and per-item errors.

concepts.title: Adaptive chunk sizing
concepts.mechanism: map_batches adapts bounded chunk length from observed admission-to-completion-callback time, including admission/queue/serialization and preceding callbacks. Growth/shrink is constrained to roughly 2x per feedback step.
concepts.applicability: Data-parallel jobs with uneven item costs.
concepts.risks: Feedback lags, callback delays and admission distort intrinsic task costs. Targets are heuristics, not deadlines or latency guarantees. Window-only map_adaptive does not amortize dispatch.
concepts.benchmark_method: Compare fixed chunks with heavy-tailed and sorted cost inputs; measure worker idle time and makespan.

concepts.title: Explicit shared-memory payloads
concepts.mechanism: Accept an application-owned descriptor for shared read-mostly buffers rather than repeatedly serializing bulk bytes.
concepts.applicability: Large numerical or media payloads reused by process workers.
concepts.risks: Ownership, lifetime, cleanup, mutation races, and platform behavior are harder than ordinary value passing.
concepts.benchmark_method: Sweep payload size and reuse count, measuring copies, transfer time, peak memory, and leak-free cleanup after failures.

concepts.title: Data-local worker affinity
concepts.mechanism: Route related eligible work toward workers with explicitly cached immutable data.
concepts.applicability: Repeated transformations over large models or datasets.
concepts.risks: Affinity can defeat load balancing; cache invalidation and worker death require explicit handling.
concepts.benchmark_method: Compare random and affinity placement under skew and worker restarts; record cache hit rate, transfer bytes, and tail latency.

concepts.title: Resource-class budgets
concepts.mechanism: Use explicit classes such as database, CPU, disk, or accelerator to enforce separate concurrency permits.
concepts.applicability: Tasks contending for a small external connection pool or a single specialized device.
concepts.risks: Tasks needing multiple classes can deadlock unless acquisition order and atomic reservation are specified.
concepts.benchmark_method: Build mixed-resource synthetic jobs, verify simultaneous-use bounds, and test cyclic acquisition requests.

concepts.title: Cooperative cancellation tokens
concepts.mechanism: Expose an opt-in cancellation signal that long-running callables can poll at application-defined safe points.
concepts.applicability: Long loops, multipart downloads, and user-interruptible transformations.
concepts.risks: Callables must cooperate, cleanup is application-specific, and cross-process tokens add synchronization cost.
concepts.benchmark_method: Cancel at each safe-point boundary and measure stop latency, cleanup correctness, and polling overhead.

concepts.title: Explicit shutdown escalation
concepts.mechanism: Offer a separately named process-only escalation path after graceful waiting, with impact made explicit to the caller.
concepts.applicability: Operators handling stuck process workers in controlled service teardown.
concepts.risks: Killing a worker can lose buffered writes, corrupt shared resources, and affect unrelated tasks in the same pool.
concepts.benchmark_method: Use isolated subprocess fixtures with stuck workers and durable markers; verify bounded teardown and report collateral failures.

concepts.title: Retry budgets and backoff
concepts.mechanism: Add an explicit retry wrapper for declared retryable failures, with attempt limits, jitter, and a global time budget.
concepts.applicability: Idempotent calls to transiently failing dependencies.
concepts.risks: Retries can duplicate side effects and amplify overload; admission limits must include retried work.
concepts.benchmark_method: Use scripted failure sequences and a fake clock, then outage recovery load tests measuring attempts per successful operation.

concepts.title: Dependency circuit breakers
concepts.mechanism: Stop new calls to a failing explicit dependency for a cooldown, then admit bounded probes.
concepts.applicability: A shared remote service failure that otherwise consumes all workers.
concepts.risks: Bad failure classification creates unnecessary outages; synchronized probes can create recovery spikes.
concepts.benchmark_method: Fault a local service, recover it, and record rejected calls, wasted work, probe counts, and recovery delay.

concepts.title: In-flight duplicate coalescing
concepts.mechanism: For declared equivalent pure tasks, share one execution among multiple subscribers with independent result views.
concepts.applicability: Repeated read-only computation for the same immutable input.
concepts.risks: Hash collisions, mutable inputs, and cancellation ownership can break correctness; shared failures affect all subscribers.
concepts.benchmark_method: Submit duplicates and near-duplicates concurrently, verify exactly the expected underlying calls, and test subscriber cancellation.

concepts.title: Explicit result caching
concepts.mechanism: Cache successful outputs only for caller-declared pure operations with versioned keys and expiry.
concepts.applicability: Expensive deterministic transformations with frequent reuse.
concepts.risks: Stale data, sensitive result retention, unbounded memory, and invalidation costs may outweigh runtime savings.
concepts.benchmark_method: Use controlled hit rates, mutated inputs, and version changes; compare total resource cost including cache memory.

concepts.title: Idempotency metadata
concepts.mechanism: Carry application-supplied operation identifiers into retry or durable adapters without pretending the executor can make a side effect atomic.
concepts.applicability: Writes to services that support their own idempotency keys.
concepts.risks: A key alone does not create exactly-once execution. Recipient retention windows and payload equality rules matter.
concepts.benchmark_method: Crash between a fake side effect and acknowledgement; verify duplicate suppression in the recipient and document unsupported windows.

concepts.title: Dependency DAG execution
concepts.mechanism: Build a separate orchestration layer that releases a task only after declared predecessor futures satisfy its dependency policy.
concepts.applicability: Multi-stage workflows with fan-out and fan-in.
concepts.risks: Cycles, failure fan-out, retained intermediates, and worker-blocking dependency waits need separate semantics.
concepts.benchmark_method: Generate acyclic graphs with known critical paths and failure points; test cycle rejection, cancellation fan-out, and retained memory.

concepts.title: Checkpointed workflow outputs
concepts.mechanism: Persist versioned outputs of completed DAG nodes through an explicit storage adapter and resume only compatible work.
concepts.applicability: Long workflows where recomputing completed stages is expensive.
concepts.risks: Checkpoint writes are not atomic with external side effects; privacy, version drift, corruption, and partial commits require policy.
concepts.benchmark_method: Inject termination before and after checkpoint boundaries and verify recovered outputs, repeated work, and storage overhead.

concepts.title: Remote executor adapter
concepts.mechanism: Implement an explicit transport and authentication boundary for submitting supported tasks to a remote worker system.
concepts.applicability: Work larger than a single host or requiring specialized machines.
concepts.risks: Network partitions, credential management, data disclosure, and non-portable callables fundamentally change the trust model.
concepts.benchmark_method: Test loss, delay, duplicate messages, authentication failure, and reconnect behavior against a local test server before external deployment.

concepts.title: Durable recovery adapter
concepts.mechanism: Add durable admission, leases, acknowledgements, and recovery to a separate service-backed layer rather than the base in-memory executor.
concepts.applicability: Work that must survive client or worker-process loss.
concepts.risks: Durable storage does not create exactly-once side effects; split-brain leases and schema upgrades complicate correctness.
concepts.benchmark_method: Inject client, worker, broker, and storage failures independently and publish an explicit survival and duplication matrix.

concepts.title: Structured execution event journal
concepts.mechanism: Emit bounded lifecycle events with task IDs, decision reasons, and monotonic timestamps through a nonblocking sink.
concepts.applicability: Postmortem debugging and trace analysis beyond aggregated profiles.
concepts.risks: Slow sinks must not block scheduler progress; dropped events and sensitive metadata need explicit handling.
concepts.benchmark_method: Overload the sink and verify bounded queue memory, drop counters, task correctness, and measured instrumentation overhead.

concepts.title: Trace-context integration
concepts.mechanism: Add an optional adapter for propagating explicitly selected trace context through threads and processes.
concepts.applicability: Services already using distributed tracing.
concepts.risks: Implicit context transfer may expose sensitive fields, and span completion during cancellation can leak resources.
concepts.benchmark_method: Link a request trace to child tasks, including failed and cancelled work; measure span overhead and verify no payload capture.

concepts.title: Deterministic decision replay
concepts.mechanism: Replay recorded policy inputs and observations through a seeded policy to explain route choices offline.
concepts.applicability: Reproducing routing regressions without rerunning expensive work.
concepts.risks: Decision replay cannot reproduce OS scheduling or reconstruct unobserved counterfactual timings.
concepts.benchmark_method: Compare repeated replays byte-for-byte and verify a controlled policy change alters only expected decisions.

concepts.title: Policy and workload version provenance
concepts.mechanism: Stamp profiles and benchmark outputs with policy configuration, code revision, workload version, and environment metadata.
concepts.applicability: Comparing results across releases or reusing persisted observations.
concepts.risks: Identifiers must not expose secrets; an unchanged function name does not imply unchanged semantics.
concepts.benchmark_method: Change one code or configuration dimension per trial and verify provenance changes and incompatible profile rejection.

concepts.title: Versioned profile persistence
concepts.mechanism: Save and reload validated aggregate profiles through an opt-in format with environment and workload compatibility checks.
concepts.applicability: Repeated short-lived jobs where relearning on every launch is expensive.
concepts.risks: Stale or tampered profiles can degrade decisions; shared files require atomic writes and privacy controls.
concepts.benchmark_method: Test round-trip, truncated files, unknown schema versions, concurrent writers, and warm-start benefit versus stale-profile regret.

concepts.title: Profile cardinality limits
concepts.mechanism: Keep at most max_profile_keys task-key buckets, evict least-recently-updated buckets, count evictions, and validate nonempty keys of at most 256 characters.
concepts.applicability: Long-lived services or callers tempted to use one unique key per request.
concepts.risks: Eviction discards useful learning and can bias against rare work; completion recency differs from request recency. The cap does not bound caller-retained snapshots.
concepts.benchmark_method: Generate many unique and recurring keys and verify bounded memory, eviction behavior, and hit-rate effects.

concepts.title: Shadow policy evaluation
concepts.mechanism: Run a candidate decision function on recorded inputs while the trusted policy remains responsible for actual routing.
concepts.applicability: Comparing policy decisions before an opt-in rollout.
concepts.risks: Shadow routes lack counterfactual outcomes; agreement is not proof of performance or safety.
concepts.benchmark_method: Measure decision disagreement and shadow overhead, then validate promising candidates with authorized live A/B trials.

concepts.title: Policy decision guardrails
concepts.mechanism: Extend existing output and process-eligibility validation with an explicitly bounded decision interface and opt-in fallback for slow or faulty plugins.
concepts.applicability: Third-party or more complex learned policies.
concepts.risks: Time-bounding arbitrary synchronous Python code is difficult; fallback behavior must not silently change side-effect semantics.
concepts.benchmark_method: Inject invalid results, exceptions, and slow decisions; verify deterministic failures or approved fallback without duplicate execution.

concepts.title: Workload equivalence checks
concepts.mechanism: Attach benchmark-only output digests or domain validators so timing comparisons also prove equivalent useful results.
concepts.applicability: Optimizations that batch, cache, route, or serialize differently.
concepts.risks: Checksums can collide and approximate numerical outputs need domain tolerances; validation cost must be separated.
concepts.benchmark_method: Intentionally corrupt one implementation and ensure the benchmark rejects its result regardless of speed.

concepts.title: Explicit hostile-code boundary
concepts.mechanism: Design any untrusted-code support as a separate sandbox integration with a defined threat model and resource restrictions.
concepts.applicability: A future service executing code supplied by mutually untrusted users.
concepts.risks: Local processes and policy plugins are not security sandboxes; unrestricted pickle and code execution remain dangerous.
concepts.benchmark_method: Use a reviewed sandbox threat model and isolation tests for filesystem, network, resources, and cross-tenant access.

concepts.title: Interpreter-pool backend
concepts.mechanism: Add an optional backend gated on a supported Python interpreter-pool API and explicit compatible-callable declarations.
concepts.applicability: Multi-core Python work on runtimes offering separate interpreter workers.
concepts.risks: Extension module compatibility, object isolation, serialization, and Python-version support differ from threads.
concepts.benchmark_method: Run an importability and extension compatibility matrix, then compare equivalent workloads with process and thread backends.

concepts.title: Free-threaded runtime awareness
concepts.mechanism: Include runtime build and GIL state in environment metadata and test routing assumptions separately on free-threaded builds.
concepts.applicability: Applications adopting Python builds that allow concurrent Python execution in threads.
concepts.risks: Removing one bottleneck does not make arbitrary shared-state code thread-safe; native extensions can alter runtime behavior.
concepts.benchmark_method: Run identical correct thread-safe workloads on each build, recording GIL state, extensions, memory, and total throughput.

concepts.title: Accelerator batch backend
concepts.mechanism: Create a dedicated opt-in backend that batches compatible jobs around a caller-supplied accelerator runner.
concepts.applicability: GPU or other device workloads with high launch overhead and bounded device memory.
concepts.risks: Device memory exhaustion, kernel asynchrony, shape compatibility, and cancellation differ from CPU futures.
concepts.benchmark_method: Use explicit synchronization around measurements and sweep batch size, shape, device memory, and end-to-end latency.

concepts.title: Native-thread oversubscription budgets
concepts.mechanism: Let applications declare native parallelism per task and coordinate executor concurrency with library thread limits.
concepts.applicability: Numerical libraries that start multiple native threads inside each submitted task.
concepts.risks: Environment variables may need to be set before imports; global settings can affect unrelated work.
concepts.benchmark_method: Compare nested thread counts across worker settings and record total runnable threads, CPU utilization, and throughput.

concepts.title: Cost-aware scheduling objective
concepts.mechanism: Combine latency with explicitly supplied compute or remote-service prices under a caller-chosen objective and budget.
concepts.applicability: Work where a cheaper slower backend may be acceptable.
concepts.risks: Prices and billing granularity can change; a weighted score may hide violations of hard spending limits.
concepts.benchmark_method: Use a frozen price fixture and workload trace, report both raw latency and cost, and verify budget constraints separately.

concepts.title: Energy-aware scheduling experiments
concepts.mechanism: Study measured energy per useful completion as a separate experimental objective under controlled hardware conditions.
concepts.applicability: Batch jobs where energy efficiency matters more than minimum latency.
concepts.risks: Wall time is not energy; external power measurement and machine isolation are needed for credible conclusions.
concepts.benchmark_method: Use a calibrated meter or validated hardware counters, report idle subtraction and uncertainty, and repeat complete runs.

concepts.title: Offline contextual policy training
concepts.mechanism: Train a small interpretable policy from consented benchmark features and evaluate it on held-out workload families before deployment.
concepts.applicability: Stable, well-characterized workloads where a simple EWMA is insufficient.
concepts.risks: Confounding, counterfactual data gaps, overfitting, and deployment drift can produce confident wrong routes.
concepts.benchmark_method: Split by workload family and machine, compare with simple hints and EWMA, and report regret plus out-of-distribution fallback behavior.

concepts.title: Static advisory analysis
concepts.mechanism: Offer opt-in diagnostics for obvious importability and serialization hazards without executing the user task.
concepts.applicability: Developers moving code from threads to processes.
concepts.risks: Static inspection cannot prove process safety, purity, or performance; diagnostics must remain advisory.
concepts.benchmark_method: Use a corpus of closures, top-level functions, bound objects, and dynamic callables; report false positives and false negatives.

concepts.title: Async application bridge
concepts.mechanism: Provide a tested integration recipe or adapter that offloads blocking admission and bridges concurrent futures into an event loop.
concepts.applicability: Async services reusing synchronous CPU or blocking I/O functions.
concepts.risks: Calling bounded submit on the event-loop thread can stall it; cancellation on one side may not stop running work on the other.
concepts.benchmark_method: Run an event-loop heartbeat under saturated submission, cancellations, and teardown; verify responsiveness and no orphan tasks.

concepts.title: Worker initializer and warmup hooks
concepts.mechanism: Expose explicit backend-specific initialization for read-only expensive resources with predictable failure reporting.
concepts.applicability: Model loading or connection setup performed once per worker.
concepts.risks: Initialization can leak credentials, block startup, or leave a broken pool; process-local connections must not be inherited blindly.
concepts.benchmark_method: Measure cold-start and steady-state latency and inject initializer failure, worker restart, and cleanup paths.

concepts.title: Fail-fast task groups
concepts.mechanism: Create an opt-in group abstraction that cancels pending siblings after one failure while collecting running-task outcomes.
concepts.applicability: Independent subtasks whose results are useful only when all succeed.
concepts.risks: Running siblings keep executing; discarding their errors or assuming side effects rolled back would be incorrect.
concepts.benchmark_method: Inject one failure among queued and running siblings and verify cancellation attempts, complete error reporting, and bounded cleanup.

concepts.title: Removable bounded dispatch queue
concepts.mechanism: Use executor-owned removable per-backend FIFO queues and bounded dispatch slots. Raw backend callbacks only enqueue completion notifications; an owned completion pump avoids backend-manager lock inversion during redispatch.
concepts.applicability: Long-running services facing repeated submit-and-cancel traffic while workers are blocked.
concepts.risks: Normal completion delivery is serialized; slow or waiting callbacks can delay the executor. Process dispatch commits cancellation early. Physical scheduling item bounds do not bound payload bytes, preempt running work, isolate callbacks, prevent dependency deadlocks or guarantee implicit interpreter-exit equivalence.
concepts.benchmark_method: Block workers while retaining many cancelled Futures; verify queued payload weakrefs are released and physical retained/dispatch counts stay bounded. Exercise cancel/dispatch races, broken process pools, backend lock inversion, result/payload release and explicit shutdown.

concepts.title: Registered JSON task framework
concepts.mechanism: An application-defined callable allowlist with JSON input discovery and validation, nonblocking bounded thread execution, retained result records, and explicit queued cancellation and cleanup.
concepts.applicability: Trusted applications needing task IDs and bounded JSON lifecycle management outside the Executor API.
concepts.risks: Not a sandbox, durable queue, authorization service, or RSS bound. Running code cannot be killed. Result validation occurs after side effects. Retained records must be forgotten.
concepts.benchmark_method: Hold a worker, saturate pending and retained-record budgets, cancel and forget queued work repeatedly, and verify no extra backend admission until wrappers drain. Verify validation, result limits, shutdown, and errors deterministically.

concepts.title: Optional MCP stdio adapter
concepts.mechanism: A separately imported optional official-SDK adapter maps MCP tools and resources to an explicit registered task service and read-only concept discovery over stdio.
concepts.applicability: Trusted local MCP hosts that need to submit and inspect bounded registered Python tasks without arbitrary code execution tools.
concepts.risks: No authentication or tenant isolation. A client can invoke every registered task and read retained results. SDK parsing and callable memory are outside JSON retention limits. Running tasks may delay process exit.
concepts.benchmark_method: Use the official client against a real stdio subprocess: initialize, discover tools/resources, submit, inspect results, cancel queued work, forget records, query metrics/catalog, reject malformed and unregistered requests, and verify shutdown.

concepts.title: Bounded transferable workload profiles
concepts.mechanism: Successful opt-in thread wall/current-thread CPU samples, exact numeric input summaries, hardware feature metadata, and observational concurrency buckets are exported/imported as strictly validated bounded schema-v1 JSON.
concepts.applicability: Explicit opt-in repeated workloads with comparable inputs and constrained execution budgets.
concepts.risks: Profiles are data, not trusted performance promises. No per-task RSS or built-in process runtime measurements; no pickle or callable/input serialization. Observational concurrency is not a controlled scaling experiment.
concepts.benchmark_method: Verify JSON limits/privacy/schema rejection and genuine clock provenance; compare timings with and without instrumentation and sample intervals.

concepts.title: Hardware-aware predictive admission
concepts.mechanism: Predictor combines CPU affinity/quota capabilities, workload evidence, objective and explicit constraints. Compatible profiles guide observed selection; foreign profiles supply uncertainty-labeled conservative priors. Admission changes within fixed backend capacities without mutating stdlib pools.
concepts.applicability: Explicit opt-in repeated workloads with comparable inputs and constrained execution budgets.
concepts.risks: Hardware feature matches are not identical machine guarantees. Cross-hardware prior is unvalidated, not learned transfer or empirical speedup. Saturation/barrier workloads can deadlock; configured constraints do not limit arbitrary memory.
concepts.benchmark_method: Compare no-profile, compatible-profile and foreign-profile starts on independently controlled workloads; record raw seeded results, hard-cap invariants, negative speedups and local-measurement refinement.

concepts.title: Explicit offline configuration calibration
concepts.mechanism: Evaluate explicit caller-owned calibration fixtures over bounded configurations. Exhaustive calibration minimizes mean objective; budgeted median successive halving selects the best comparable finalist. Reject correctness/resource/latency failures and validate frozen selections on independent holdout fixtures.
concepts.applicability: Applications with safe repeatable calibration fixtures that can amortize measured configuration cost before running ordinary work.
concepts.risks: Caller owns idempotence, representative inputs and holdout independence. Budgets count evaluator calls, not elapsed-time enforcement; measured caps filter observations rather than impose OS limits. No implicit task replay, global optimum or online convergence guarantee. Saved schema-v2 configurations bind scheduler/strategy revisions, workload, runtime and hardware identity.
concepts.benchmark_method: Use deterministic callback fixtures to verify consent, bounds, errors, caps and selection; then compare actual representative workload runs with equal stdlib algorithm/resource/search grids, separate calibration/hold-out seeds, exact provenance and all configuration cost.

concepts.title: Evidence-gated executor adoption
concepts.mechanism: Evaluate caller-consented repeatable fixtures with equivalent bounded stdlib/intelligent budgets. Freeze training winners before a fixed randomized paired holdout. Require exact median log-speedup evidence versus fixed and tuned stdlib, practical margin, noise/correctness/resource/regression gates and empirical discovery-cost amortization.
concepts.applicability: Incremental adoption decisions for explicitly representative independent fixtures, with retained stdlib fallback and exact-mode compatibility checks.
concepts.risks: Fixture consent does not establish idempotence or statistical independence. Median paired gains are not mean throughput, tail or cumulative-savings guarantees. Repeated experiments need separate multiplicity control; resource observations are not hard OS limits. No live-task replay or automatic deployment.
concepts.benchmark_method: Test controlled positive, null, noisy, failed, missing-resource, stale-mode and process-consent cases; publish every outcome of fixed representative fixture experiments with all raw scalar measurements and discovery cost.

concepts.title: Bounded sanitized routing explanations
concepts.mechanism: Opt-in immutable accepted-routing records retained in a bounded ring with fixed-category cumulative counters, backend/reason and exact pre-admission scheduler counts. No callable, input, output, exception, key or custom-policy text is retained.
concepts.applicability: Inspecting why accepted work chose a backend while keeping data capture explicit and bounded.
concepts.risks: Metadata has overhead and is not proof of causal speedup or CPU/RSS usage. Rejected submissions are not accepted-routing records; counters and trace snapshots from separate calls can represent different instants.
concepts.benchmark_method: Verify ring eviction, fixed counter cardinality, immutable concurrent snapshots, no object retention, stable reasons under admission contention, and trace-enabled cancellation/shutdown cycles.
